utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good afternoon to everyone. May I have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, assisted by Crispian Smith, Case Manager.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic and Eugene O'Sullivan appearing for Stanisic Defence this afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence, Igor Pantelic and Dragan Krgovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. And if there are no preliminary matters to concern us, could the Usher please escort the witness back to the stand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May the record show that Mr. Cvijetic has joined us, in Stanisic Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Vlaski. Before I -- I invite Ms. Korner to continue her examination-in-chief, I remind you you're still on your oath. You are may take your seat. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Vlaski, we were looking at the barricade incident yesterday, beginning of March. I would like you to have a look, please, at a newsreel footage, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Armed and masked people are blocking traffic. In the city, around 20 barricades have been put up. The shooting lasted the whole night, particularly in the municipality of Novo Sarajevo. Behind the barricades made of transport vehicles, there are civilians armed from head to foot who told foreign companies that the reason for barricades was the murder which took place in Bascarsija the day before. Ten minutes before midnight, Sarajevo Television broadcast information by our journalist who noticed stopping of trolley-buses and putting up of the barricade at the beginning of Mice Sokolovica Street. Police patrol returned in front of the pointed barrels. People were killed during last night fire-fight. Now it only has been confirmed that Pandurevic and two more citizens were killed on the barricades. Foreign agencies said that there had been six people killed. "In the morning, traffic was blocked in the city, schools didn't work. They didn't even let ... "On behalf of Crisis Staff, Rajko Dukic, chairperson of SDS executive committee, spoke about the reasons to put up barricades, demands by Serb people and activities of the Crisis Staff: "A lot happened over the last couple of days what incited, provoked Serbian people who unfortunately have chosen the only possible option and that is to take to the barricades, and one can easily say, to bring attention to something that would be normal in a democratic and civilised society, and that because of one's independence, identity, and sovereignty, nobody has the right to deprive somebody else of that same right. The Serbian people did not expect that in addition there would -- their flag would be shot at, which is what unfortunately happened yesterday at 1600 hours, so to speak, in the centre of Sarajevo. "The demands of the Serbian people from Sarajevo and the whole territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina have been manifested through the Crisis Staff under the conditions that have certainly be pointed out. According to the communiqué of the information service of the BiH Presidency, the demands of the Serbian people were only partially met. The Crisis Staff ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Vlaski, who are the people flanking Rajko Dukic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see anybody applauding Mr. Dukic. I can see that this is a press conference.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, flanking, on either side. Like the Judges.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a different matter. They were the participants in the conference, together Mr. Rajko Dukic, the person who spoke of this unfortunate incident. To his right is Mr. Todor Dutina and Velibor Ostojic, the minister of information, to his left. He was on the government of what was still, at the time, the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Mr. Dukic was the president of the executive board of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who was Mr. Dutina?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall what his official title at the time was. I know that he was a representative there. But what his actual position was, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Yes, we can stop the video, thank you. I have just got a couple of other things to ask you, Mr. Vlaski. First is to look at a document -- firstly, you listened to an intercept yesterday. This is one of the ones that is on our 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we have up, please, 1056.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, we lost the LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, so we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's back again. All right. Could we have up on the screen, please, 65 ter 1056.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's not back again on our side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: We're also blank. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do Your Honours want me to continue? I don't whether ... all right. Your Honours, before we look at this one, can I -- I'm not clear what the situation was. You allowed me to use this video. Am I allowed to exhibit it? It wasn't on the 65 ter list. No, this is one -- you gave me permission to use this because it was open source material. But I'm just asking whether I can exhibit it, because I'd like to exhibit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It would be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So Your Honours would like an application in writing to add this to our 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I expect so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P980 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, first of all, sir, you listened to this intercept, is that right, which is said to between Stojan Zupljanin and Mico Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you able to recognise the voices?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As those of Mr. Zupljanin and Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This was on the 2nd of March of 1992, and the conversation refers to the barricades.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we look, please, at the second page in English, and I think it's the second page -- yes, it's the second page also in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Stojan Zupljanin says: "We're a listening a bit to how things are going over there." And Mico Stanisic says: "Well, you can hear." "We are following and listening," as they say, "and waiting for further instructions." Now you said the barricades were a spontaneous incident in Sarajevo for the Serbs to, as it were, protect themselves. Do you know why, because you were with Mico Stanisic in the Holiday Inn during this period, Stojan Zupljanin was saying, We're waiting for further instructions?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was logical, since the security situation was so complex. I said earlier on that it was a political assassination and that's one of the gravest qualifications of crime which calls for an appropriate reaction on the part of the authority, and it wasn't forthcoming. The police didn't show the willingness to do its job, and the barricades were a response to a political assassination. The barricades had not been organised before the murder took place but afterwards, and it had occurred as a spontaneous event. It is difficult in moments such as these when such a large overbearing incident happens to ease the tensions that had come to the fore in the country anyway. An adequate reaction on the part of the Ministry of the Interior and the authorities in general to launch an investigation to identify the perpetrators and punish them, such a formal intervention, especially of the Presidency, was not forthcoming.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm sorry, I didn't want to interrupt the witness. But we are facing a lot of problems now without the LiveNote because we cannot follow what -- I mean ... we need to watch the document at the same time and ... the LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I gather that it's going to take about ten minutes for this -- for the technical problem to be corrected. So in the interests of the Defence who is particularly handicapped, perhaps we should rise. --- Break taken at 2.33 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Vlaski, I would like you to concentrate, please, on the question and not make a speech. The question I asked you is why, if this is a spontaneous outbreak in Sarajevo, Stojan Zupljanin should be saying - could we go back to the intercept - We're waiting for further instructions. And then Mico Stanisic says, Be ready and we'll be in touch. Zupljanin: For the most part, everything is ready on our side. Stanisic: Yes, we are waiting for a sign. If a total blockade is needed, all the rest, it will be done. Now, if this is a spontaneous outbreak in Sarajevo, why is Stojan Zupljanin in Banja Luka awaiting instructions from Mico Stanisic to set up a blockade in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is only logical. An organised response had to match an organised incident. If somebody organises a political assassination and if this is done by the criminal underworld which is in collusion with the political leadership, then such a murder can happen anywhere in the country. This wasn't a murder as the result of a -- a brawl in a cafe. This was a wedding party which was sporting a Serb flag, and they were the object of the attack, and so there was message behind that. Action will always provoke a reaction.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is about the fourth or fifth time you have described this as a political assassination. You had a chance to listen to your interview in Banja Luka. Do you agree this is the first time in this court that you have described this killing as a political assassination?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, we didn't speak about this incident in specific terms. It has all -- it bears all of the hallmarks of a political assassination, and I have a degree -- I hold a degree in criminology and I know what I'm talking about and I can give you a definition of a political assassination.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The only question was: Do you agree -- you never mentioned the words "political assassination" in the interview in Banja Luka when this very incident was discussed. And the answer to that, you've already said, is yes. You yourself, you told this Court, were skiing at the time that the murder of the wedding guest took place. How, therefore, by the following day did you know this was a political assassination?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- it was evidently a political assassination. We had intelligence to the effect that the party of democratic action had mobilised criminal structures in the city of Sarajevo. Every criminal structure was in control of a specific neighbourhood in the city of Sarajevo. I can explain to you in great detail which particular criminal structure had control under which quarter of the town and was headed by which criminal individual. We had intelligence to the effect that there was disagreement within the MUP as to why criminal structures were being involved in certain activities. This was a conflict between Mr. Alibabic and Dautbasic about whether the criminals should be involved into this or not. Mr. Alibabic was a professional and was opposed to this, and Mr. Dautbasic said that if need be, he would even forge an alliance with the devil himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You told us you went skiing, you got the phone call when you returned on the Sunday afternoon, and you went straight over to the premises of, first of all, the Deputies Club in the Assembly and then to the Holiday Inn. How, by that stage, did you acquire all this information about this being a political killing?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only too clear. The policeman who was right on the spot when the murder took place, he identified the murderer and the murderer was not apprehended by the police at all. In other words, the police was aware of his identity and was protecting the murderer and that's where the problem lay. Had the police reacted in a professional way, right on the spot, this response would not have ensued. Had we received information about the apprehension of the perpetrator, the events would have taken a different course that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's line 8 -- sorry, it's page 8, line 19, in transcript we have a following sentence: Mr. Alibabic was and if need be he would even forge alliance with the devil himself. I believe that this witness didn't say this particular sentence, and I would kindly ask my learned friend to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What, that Mr. Alibabic would forge an alliance with the Devil himself; is that what you say he didn't say? Anyhow, Mr. Vlaski speaks some English so perhaps he could tell us.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that Mr. Alibabic did that, but Mr. Dautbasic did. Mr. Alibabic was a professional, and he was opposed to such an alliance with the criminals. And it Mr. Dautbasic who said that he would forge an alliance even with the devil himself, let alone with criminals.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was under the impression -- I was under the impression, before we leave the intercept, that it already had been made an exhibit, but through Mr. Zepinic. But I'm told not. So, in which case, can I have it made an exhibit now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we took the -- there is a ruling under which conditions the intercept can be -- can be admitted. This is not the case. The witness was not a party, he was not -- he was not present at the time, nor was he -- was he privy to the contents of this particular conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That was my recollection, Mr. Zecevic. On what basis are you seeking to have this admitted, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I understand it, on the 2nd of March -- Mr. Zecevic, you know, Mr. Zecevic, it's polite to sit down if somebody else is standing up. Yes, my understanding is this conversation took place on the 2nd of March at the time when this witness and Mr. Stanisic are at the Holiday Inn together, or in the same place. In addition to that, he's able to speak as to the contents and he's able to recognise the voices. Can I say, I can't think of any more criteria for making a document admissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, the ruling that the Chamber has made is that where a person -- although a witness might purport to identify the voices on a transcript -- on an intercept, if he was -- if he -- was himself not a party to the exchange, or was present, was otherwise present, then it is not admissible by -- through that witness. It may be admissible otherwise. Do I understand you to be saying that the testimony of this witness is that he was, in fact, present?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That he was there in the Holiday Inn with Mico Stanisic. He gave evidence yesterday. I don't know whether he can say he was actually present at the time of the call. I -- probably not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Consistent with -- with the ruling that the Chamber has made -- [French on English Channel]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we have English. Could we have English, please. I didn't -- I'm afraid because the French was going on while Your Honour was talking, I didn't catch what Your Honour said. Was the ruling that it was admitted or not admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That it is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P981 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want you, finally, to look, please, at a letter that you were shown in interview, which is -- is -- is 65 ter number 3370. It's dated 10th of October -- I'll just wait for the English to come up. It's dated 10th of October, 1994. And it's addressed to the Government of the Republika Srpska, to Mr. Brdjanin. Did you know Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had the opportunity to meet him, as a deputy in the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, after the first multi-party elections.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And the letter is signed by Mr. Kesic. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And, effectively, what it is, is it's asking for an apartment to be allocated to you. But it's the middle paragraph I want to ask you about. He was amongst the first people in the former state security of the former Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP to organise the Serbian personnel in order to oppose the Croatian-Muslim coalition, as it's put. Is that an accurate description of your activities during the course of 1991 and early 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that I was in that group of desperate people who were working in an institution that was called the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and who were completely marginalised and who had a need to self-organise for reasons which were then later verified and recognised by international agreements.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now can you answer my question, please. Is that description an accurate one?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was that -- deserving that, in 1994, I was forced to temporarily resolve my housing issue. Had I really been deserving, somebody would have adequately dealt with that matter before that. But in 1994, at the end of the war practically, I was seeking a temporary solution for my housing problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I'll ask for the third time, please, Mr. Vlaski. Mr. Kesic describes you as one of the -- among the first people in the former state security to organise Serbian personnel in order to oppose what is described as the Croatian-Muslim coalition. Were you one of the first people to organise the Serbs within the MUP against the non-Serb members?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not organise against other members of the MUP. We organised ourselves in order to protect, as I said, our personal and professional interests, as well as the interests of the people that we represented. Yes, and I was in that group.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P982, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You told the Court yesterday, in one of your many speeches, about the Muslims and Croats - and this is at page 6350 of the transcript: "That the SDA and the HDZ in the MUP played with me, humiliated me." Is that what you feel about what happened to you in the MUP during 1991 and early 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The best illustration for that would be my appointment and the issuing of the decision and the abolishment of that post. I mean, that was only just me, but that was the fate of many others. But I had the misfortune, let's say, to experience what I did experience, not for some personal problems that I had with those people, but because of nationalist and political reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe I heard Ms. Korner said, No further questions, but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I did. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It was not recorded in the transcript. That's why I wanted to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I wasn't sure either, Mr. Zecevic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Vlaski. I'm going to put a couple of questions to you. But, first of all, I have to ask you, because you and me are speaking the same language, to make a pause so that the interpreters would have time to translate. I'm going to show you, yesterday, during the day, you talked about the situation in the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. You talked about that today a little bit as well. I'm going to show you document 1D114. This is an inter-party agreement within the coalition of the HDZ, SDA, and the SDS, from January 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... please give to the witness a binder of the documents in order to facilitate for the witness only, if there is no objection from my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have it on the screen, but I can also give you a hard copy. You can see that the heading of the document states in handwriting, January 1991. And then, in item 2, we have a list of the leading posts in the Ministry of the Interior. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you can see, under B, deputy of the minister. And then on the one hand it says SDS and then it says Zepinic. And then E we have assistant to the minister for crime fighting SDS. And then we have Momcilo Mandic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that corresponds to the situation in the MUP after 1991, in the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it corresponds for the most part. There are elements here which were not verified until later. I'm talking about some personnel options.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I asked you deliberately only about these first two. Mr. Zepinic and Momcilo Mandic. Do you agree that they really performed those duties, as stated here on this list?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did perform those duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Under letter L, there is the assistant -- or the deputy for the under-secretary for the State Security Service, then it says that the post belongs to the SDS. And then we see the name Boro Susic, I think. If I understood your testimony correctly from yesterday and today, precisely that is the post that you were supposed to be appointed to and were appointed to but then that post, after your appointment, was deleted from the classification of posts in the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I give an explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, but I'm just asking you to go slowly, please. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Zepinic was appointed deputy minister from the ranks of the Serbian people, and he was nominated by the Serbian Democratic Party which won a share of the power after the multi-party elections. Mr. Zepinic was a member of the Ministry of the Interior, and he was among the professionals, according to his experience as well as his education. Mr. Momcilo Mandic did finish police schools. He worked in the judiciary after that -- in the police and then in the judiciary, and he was dealing with the issues of crime. So because of his professional qualifications, he was elected or appointed as assistant minister as opposed to the person from the ranks of the SDA, who was a man, who was highly educated but performed work which had nothing to do with the police. He had worked in our health centre in the process of recruiting staff into the police forces.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to repeat his last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The interpreters need the witness to repeat his last sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want to analyse any further. I could provide a broader analysis for each of the posts in the Ministry of the Interior. I said about the assistant minister for uniformed police, from the ranks the SDA, a person was appointed for that post, of a high education, but without any experience or any expertise for the duties that such a post would imply.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I would just kindly ask you for the name of that assistant from the SDA.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Avdo Hebib.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The organisational structure of the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was customary in those areas, and it had two parts: Public security and state security. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: State security, where you worked, was headed by the under-secretary for state security. I am talking about the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that post, the under-secretary for state security, was assigned, pursuant to this coalition agreement, to the HDZ, and Mr. Branko Kvesic came to that post.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kvesic assumed that post.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You were the chief of the 5th Administration in the State Security Service; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a lower ranking organisational unit that is part of the state security organisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You were supposed to be given a decision as deputy -- as -- deputy under-secretary for state security, and you were supposed to be the assistant to Branko Kvesic and the main operative in the State Security Service. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. May I just give a slightly more detailed explanation for this organisational structure?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can, but please be concise.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This coalition agreement, as we can see, followed the multi-party elections, and it was supposed to be the parameter for the distribution of the key positions in the institutions of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which it still was at the time. The under-secretary for state security was appointed to Branko Kvesic, who was a representative of the HDZ, and represented the Croatian people. Pursuant to the agreement, the deputy under-secretary for state security should have been assigned to a representative of the Serbian people, and that person was supposed to be nominated by the Serbian Democratic Party. This post was not filled for half a year, and that was a deliberate action by the coalition partners who tried in all possible ways to obstruct this particular appointment. The reasons for such conduct could be seen in the fact that the existing rules on classification of posts, according to the laws in effect at the time, the deputy under-secretary is actually the most important position in state security. The person assigned to that post is responsible for the work of the operative force in Bosnia and Herzegovina. No operative measure, wire-tapping or any other kind of action, could be carried out without the knowledge of that particular person. Precisely this fact speaks to the scale of obstruction that was being carried out in relation to this service. There was no person who was professionally in charge of this particular aspect of the work. This was given to the internal agreement of representatives of the Bosniak Muslim people and the Croatian people for as long as they shared common interests. The representatives of the Serbian people were given the sole important post in that service, and that is the security for persons and facilities. This was a very difficult job because it's very easy to make mistakes in that work, whereas, that person had no influence in the shaping and performance of the most sensitive duties from the area of state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly and to summarize, you, as you have told us several times till now, never actually assumed those duties as deputy under-secretary for state security, even though that should have happened. And, in essence, on the basis of what you have told us, the Muslims, primarily, and the Croats, practically controlled the State Security Service of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina almost entirely at that time?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, the absolute control of the work and all the activities of that service was in the hands of the Muslims. I'm talking about the top leadership, because it was up to them would be done and what would be accorded significance. Serbian representatives did not have any influence at all in that area. They were even bypassed in some purely banal matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have a document here, 1D118. This is a document from March 1992. It's information about the abuses, illegalities, and manipulation by the SDS cadres in the State Security Service of the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That document is an exhibit in this case, since, I, in our conversation yesterday --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry? Madam Korner, you said something? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I asked for a number. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's 1D118.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, when I showed you that, you told me that this information was something that you were not familiar with, and that is why I'm not going to present the entire document to you. I'm going to read some of the characteristic excerpts so that you could confirm whether you agree with them or not. On page 1, it says: "Since the multi-party elections until today, the personnel policies in the State Security Service of the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was conducted by Hilmo Selimovic, Asim Dautbasic, Alibabic --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I please have the bit that you're reading out on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is page 1. It's the first -- it's the first -- the second paragraph. "The personnel police of the BiH MUP ..." Have you found that, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The personnel policy of the BiH, has been run by Hilmo Selimovic, Asim Dautbasic, Munir Alibabic, and Branko Kvesic. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the most tragedy aspect because they are at the head of the SDS. So they should have also taken it upon themselves to interpret the policies of the SDS too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A little bit lower on that page, we're looking at the fourth paragraph from the top, discusses this case of yours. And it says: "When drawing up the new structure and systematisation of the SDB in March 1991, Asim Dautbasic, Munir Alibabic, and Branko Kvesic pushed through two insignificant assistant places instead of the place of the SDB deputy under-secretary, which belonged to the SDS, according to the inter-party agreement." Isn't this correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. Because they did what they wanted, because nobody could have any influence over what they would write in the rules, that draft rules that then they would submit to the government for adoption.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, sometimes -- somewhere in the middle of that paragraph it states -- I think this is the third or fourth sentence after that paragraph, it says that Asim Dautbasic practically, from the level of the State Security Service of the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, along with the agreement of the under-secretary, completely took over the coordination of the work of the service, creating such channels of the flow of information where the SDS cadres were bypassed so that the information from the bottom to the top and the leadership of the SDA and the HDZ went exclusively by way of these two parties. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In such relations, there was no need for us even to come to work. They could have sent our salaries to us at home. We could have been out there skiing or sitting at home because we were not even needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go to the next page. We're talking about page 2 in the e-court as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The second paragraph from the top says: "With a view to enforcing discipline among certain cadres, Serb staff, various methods were applied, failure to issue rulings as prescribed in the new rules of procedures on the internal organisation of the SDB, withholding parts of completed rulings until the person was transferred to another less significant post, and, outside the SDB, attempts of classic recruitment, taking statements, et cetera." Were you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a concept which was previously planned and which had the objective of bringing the Serb staff into an unfavorable position. This was the SDA strategy, and Alija Izetbegovic wanted the Serbs to reduce them to a minority. And a way to that was to clear the state security of any Serb staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The following paragraph is paragraph number 5 on a the page. And you say that focus in the work of the service is placed almost exclusively on the operative inquiries of the activities within the SDS from the lowest organisational units to the higher levels of leadership. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fully agree. Precisely this sentence, this piece of information, prompted the press release which the -- the incumbents of the state security leadership only inform, addressing the public at large, and distancing themselves from such activities of the state organs and from such manipulations as performed by the MUP and the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The last paragraph on this page states that as of the month of May 1991, the telephone line in the Deputies Club of the SDS had been wire-tapped and so on and so forth. And, on the following page, mention is made of some secret intercepting points that had been set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is page 3 in e-court, paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you see that, and can you tell us anything about it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can recount the entire story surrounding such practice, since I was one of the persons who had extensive experience in such activities because I had been working on precisely such duties for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: First of all, speak slowly, and be very concise. Give us only the key points. Thank you. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The legislation in force regulated the application of operative and technical measures and means. They were defined by the law in very precise terms as well as with the rules governing the work of the State Security Service. However, the rules and laws were one matter, and the practice was another altogether. It was in quite an unlawful way that representatives of the leadership were eavesdropped on, the members of parliament who were duly elected, including us, I'm sure of that. Every individual who showed or exhibited any sort of activity aimed at safeguarding the interests of either the profession, the law, or national interests was the subject of the activities of this structure, which misused the means it had in order to meet the requests issued to them by their leaders. A vertical system was established from the assistant leader of state security, Mr. Dautbasic, all the way down to the lowest level of operatives who applied various operative means and measures. The matter was so dramatic that members of the Party for Democratic Action were directly involved in such unlawful activities. Representatives of the party intercepted communications from specific sights which were placed outside of state security facilities, namely in private homes and various buildings. We have documents to prove that. These same representatives of the party, having obtained, through unlawful means, various information, forwarded to Mr. Munir Alibabic these -- the same information once or twice a week. This was documented in the log-book, registering the movement of different persons. This was in the MUP building, where Mr. Alibabic was the minister. The public security forces, that's to say the police, were duty-bound to register every individual who entered the building, as well as the person they were visiting. In this particular book, we found information to the effect that three members of the Party of Democratic Action would enter the building, in the context that I'm speaking of, and bring in material. The purpose behind this was for the material to be processed and then forwarded to the political leadership and, in part, to the media. We have proof that on a weekly basis Mr. Senad Abdic, editor of "Slobodna Bosna" paper, came there routinely. They published this sort of information in order to justify the activities taken by the party leadership in relation to the Serb staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you here and put several questions to in relation to what you just told us. If my understanding of what you said is correct, and please tell me if it's not, the wire-tapping measures, the interception measures, which the State Security Service was authorised to carry out under the law and in keeping with specific procedure, in the course of 1991 and 1992, were, in actual fact, privatised in the service of the -- of a political party, namely, the SDA. Just tell me if I'm right or not.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is fully privatised in the service of the SDA, and, in part, the HDZ as well. Insofar as it was needed by the Croats or, alternatively, by the Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Moreover, if my understanding is correct, these eavesdropping measures, which were applied from, as you put it, the certain sites that had been set up ad hoc, were not applied by technicians who were employed by the State Security Service but, rather, by certain individuals who were members of the Party of Democratic Action. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not right. Expertise is required to apply these measures, as well as a series of conditions that needed to be met. In order for such an operation to be conducted, there had to be coordinated activity from a number of individuals, from telecommunications operators, and so on and so forth. Let me not go into explaining the techniques behind the work because it -- they will take us too far. The gist of the matter is that in the application of these measures SDA members were involved, and they were the ones producing the end product.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The SDA staff who yielded the end product worked together with Munir Alibabic, whom they visited once or twice weekly, at least, at the very least, in his office. That's what you told us, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Certain representatives of the Serb people were involved in this as well, who were performing their regular official duties. They also had some involvement in these unlawful activities, and they informed us of them. They were afraid of doing anything, however, because they were afraid for their own fate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You also said that Mr. Munir Alibabic, who created these documents together with his SDA colleagues, forwarded the -- some of these documents to the media, which was in violation of the regulations that were in force at the time.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were certain rules in place in relation to the media. In order for certain information to reach the media, it had to go through the analysis department first, which would decide whether the material was apt to be publicised or whether it should only be forward to the leadership staff. However, here it was Dautbasic, Alibabic, and Kvesic who decided which of the information needed to be published in the media, such as "Slobodna Bosna," or any other media that suited them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We will resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Our delay in resuming, the Bench was -- we were doing other work in the interim. Yes, please continue, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlaski, before the break, we were just about to discuss "Slobodna Bosna" and the media in general. But let me put one other question before we move to that topic. The SDA activists, who, together with Mr. Alibabic, were involved in these, as you call them, unlawful intercepting activities, can you tell me, were they individuals called Behman, Arnautovic, Skalonja, and Osman? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that very well, because I had occasion to see the names of these individuals in the book registering visitors entering the MUP building in Sarajevo. I also had occasion to see them later on, on the MUP payroll, when this became common knowledge, and their presence in the MUP was legalised by them being -- becoming employees of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go back to the media. You said that Messrs. Alibabic, Dautbasic, and Kvesic decided independently which information would be provided to the media. Can you tell us what media was involved? Was it "Muslimanski Glas," "Slobodna Bosna," and "Hercegovacki Tjednik" and similar papers?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these two as well as others; the dailies, such as the "Sarajevo Oslobodjenje."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "involved," they were used for the purposes of a propaganda war, was it not?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was part of the political, military, and media preparations for the takeover of power in Bosnia by the HDZ/SDA coalition and to the detriment of the Serb people. The representatives of this particular policy believed that they ought to be the masters in Bosnia-Herzegovina. It seems that for Bosnia-Herzegovina the relationship between the master and the servant was a historical category, and they believed that it was time for them to become masters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If my understanding of your testimony is correct, this discussion of ours, concerning 1D118, shows that you substantially or -- agree with what is contained in the document. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could discuss this particular document for days and corroborate what is stated there with various statements and documents because there is no better proof than this one to show how far Mr. Kvesic, who was at the head of the State Security Service, privatised the service. When he no longer felt that he needed to remain in Sarajevo, he brought along with him documentation concerning the service, and this was an illustration of his unlawful and unprofessional conduct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may add, it was precisely because of such actions that were taken that certain individuals committed suicide, because of what had been published about them in the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vlaski, do you know that the Party of Democratic Action, in the course of 1991, sent young men to be trained in the Croatian MUP?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. And I personally saw documents dispatching these men to the training centre in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will show you 1D123. This is a document issued by the SDA. The document is dated 11 July 1991. It is instructions for candidates, and it is addressed to the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia. Let me put one question to you before we start discussing the documents. You will see that on the right-hand side, in the heading, it says SDA - Party for Democratic Action - Sarajevo, Marsala Tita Street, 7A. Do you remember if this was, indeed, the correct address of the head office of the SDA in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was precisely their address.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The document shows that the SDA recommended that certain candidates be admitted to the centre in the Republic of Croatia. Reference is made to some sort of a mutual agreement. What is crucial, however, is that the Party of Democratic Action, as a political party, should be sending their members to such a training course for reserve policemen; whilst, at the same time, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, there existed a school where policeman could undergo training. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. This is the best illustration of such unlawful conduct. Any state, if it wants to state that it's ruled by law, then it cannot have this sort of cooperation with a neighbouring state, in this case, the Republic of Croatia, whilst bypassing the regular procedure. It is out of the ordinary and unlawful that one should organise training in this way. But this reflects the situation in which we had to operate. And it sounds somehow comical that I should even call it a state. It's a caricature of a state.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that these candidates who were sent to attend training in the Republic of Croatia also took part in the armed activities of the Croatian MUP and the ZNG against the JNA and Serbs in Croatia? Were you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite clearly, in order for such agreement to exist as is referred to herein, there would first would have to exist an agreement between the Republic of Croatia and the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Again, in this instances, as well as in other situations, the Serbs were bypassed. They should have, at the very least, been informed about it, and, of course, under the existing rules and regulations, they should have been consulted. What was happening here was the cooperation between the political leadership in Croatia and the leaderships of the HDZ and SDA in Bosnia-Herzegovina. This goes to show that the SDA party was using this channel to create an armed force of its own. This was a way for it to create its own army, through the Ministry of the Interior, which later proved to be true. Suffice it to say, that the very way in which they obtained the candidates is telling. They used the records in the possession of the Ministry of Defence where qualities of these candidates were listed for specific military disciplines. Sefer Halilovic prepared a military concept for the creation of an armed force, and it was following that particular concept that these candidates were sent to the Republic of Croatia for training.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me now show you another document by the SDA --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't believe there was an answer to the question that was asked by Defence counsel. Namely, whether the candidates who were sent to attend the training in the Republic of Croatia also took part in the armed activities of the Croatian MUP and the ZNG against the JNA and Serbs. There was no answer to that question, at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you kindly answer this question? Yes, Ms. Korner is right. Your response was quite long so I even missed it.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think this is something that was happening in a different state. I don't know for what sort of purposes they used them over there. It was a bit difficult for us to know, so I'm unable to answer that question correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Thank you. I would now like to show you document 1D00-4681. This is a document by the SDA of the 8th of July, 1991, and it bears the heading: The List of Candidates for the Training of Special Forces in the MUP of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the information, but I'm not sure whether this is P424 in this case file, MFI.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't say this last time, but I'm going say it this time. Before we go any further with these documents, two things: Firstly, has the witness ever seen it before? Second, please may I be told where exactly these documents come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, first of all, I have to show the document to the witness in order to be able to put questions to him. Secondly, on the 2nd of February of this year, in relation to a piece of correspondence by Ms. Korner, I informed Ms. Korner in writing about the sources of all the documents of Mr. Stanisic's Defence. I listed six sources from where all the documents that we have and that we are presenting in the proceedings are from. I can list those documents again. And this specific document came from the MUP of Republika Srpska, from the team for the investigation of war crimes from Banja Luka. I don't know if this is sufficient. I was hoping that this document and my letter of the 2nd of February would be sufficient so that we would have no more need to go into the sources of the documents and discuss that particular matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I explain? It is absolutely right. Your Honour will recall I raised this before in respect of some of these documents. One of the documents in particular, which was presented by Mr. Cvijetic, apparently came from a web site maintained by an accused in this Tribunal, namely -- I've forgotten what his name is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: General Praljak.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Without any attribution whatsoever as to where these documents actually come from. That's my concern. It's no good, as I say, simply saying, Our documents come from these six sources. There will be an objection to any document which comes off a web site for which there is no attribution to where these documents come from, and particularly a web site maintained by an accused in this Tribunal. Secondly, my concern is this: Not the general sources, but where each individual document about which we raise a query comes from. And I've now had a response in relation to this one. I have nothing further to say. Do I take it the previous document that you showed this witness is also from the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. And it has already been exhibited in this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Without the objection from you. Yes, the previous document is 1D123, and it has been exhibited already.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Without any objection from the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I think we may be taking some -- more interest into where these documents emanate from. However, the point still is, is has this witness - and I appreciate until he has seen it, he can't give the answer - but has he actually seen this document before? He wasn't asked in the previous case whether he had seen that document before. In the previous -- the previous document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So in answer to both of the issues that you raise Ms. Korner, each item will be dealt with it as it arises on an item-by-item basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. And, Your Honour, at the moment, I'm still waiting to hear whether the witness saw the previous document he was shown -- had seen before, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not exhibiting this -- this particular -- this previous document I'm not exhibiting with this witness because it's already exhibited by another witness. Therefore, I don't see any reason why should I ask the witness if he has seen the particular document? The witness knows about the fact that the SDA was sending candidates to -- to -- to -- MUP of Croatia for -- for the training. That is all that I wanted to elicit from the witness on that particular document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, in that case, what is the point of showing him a document without asking him whether he has seen it? You're inviting him to comment. You could have asked the question, with the greatest of respect, without showing a document whether -- which he, may I say, I should be very surprised if he has seen before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlaski, you have a document in front of you. It's a list of the candidates for training as special forces in the Republic of the Croatia MUP of the 8th of July, 1991. You've looked at the document. First, can you please tell me whether you had the opportunity to see this document before?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one specifically, no. But I did see a similar document on the same topic, which we even published in a piece of information material, in English, which we drafted in 1992, in Belgrade, with the Jugo Istok, South East agency. There is a copy done on the -- or an issue done on the topic of media manipulation; I gave that to the representatives of the OTP. Unfortunately, I didn't have copies of that publication with the documents that were included in that. The publication is called "The Chronicles of Anticipated Death," and they were sent to -- this issue was sent to many addresses in the course of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say you gave that publication to the OTP, can you tell me, when did you give it to them?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't give them that one. We did three different publication in that period on different topics. One was on military, political, and media preparation, and, in that context, the first publication published a document on this same topic. The second publication, which I did give to the Prosecution, had to do with the media manipulation coming from the west, and it documents exactly the facts which were deliberately manipulated for purposes of media manipulation, in that publication.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say it's a similar document, do you think that it's a similar document by format, or does it also refer to the same topic or that it is a list of candidates for training in special forces in special forces in the Republic of Croatia of the MUP, that document?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that document which we put in that publication does also deal with the same topic of sending special forces for training to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you look at the last page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is page 14, I think, in the e-court. Actually, it's 14 in the Serbian and perhaps already page 2 in the English. Because it's just a question of names. Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You can see that this document which lists a total of 463 persons of Muslim ethnicity is signed by Rasim Muharemovic from the SDA Sarajevo. There is a signature and a stamp. Do you know who Rasim Muharemovic was?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a person who was in charge of security issues in the SDA party.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So this gentleman, Muharemovic, was, let's say, the chief of security of the Party of Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not security in the sense that he is doing protection work, but he is organising security within the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since you had the opportunity now to look at this document, can you please tell me whether, by its contents, it's similar to the document which you included in that publication or not?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a similar document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document as an MFI document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It already is ... [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, I'm -- I was just -- it's P424. So then the Prosecution actually tendered this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no, you did. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But it's P424.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm really confused. It's P424 then it was tendered by the Prosecution and now Ms. Korner is -- is objecting for me using this document. I'm not -- I'm really -- I'm really confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I thought her objection was of a general nature, not to this specific document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can we have it then, if there is no objection, can we have it exhibited without the MFI?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... been a mistake. It was put to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I -- there seems -- I think there has been a mistake in the tendering -- I -- because I recall Mr. Draganovic was asked by the Defence about this. They asked for it to be -- it's not on our document list. You can tell. It's a Defence document. It couldn't have been put in by us. So there must be a mistake in the numbering.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. I accept, and I will not lose any more time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, indeed, I think it was marked for identification because we raised the self-same objection to it at the time it was sought to put it in, through Mr. Draganovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: P424, MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It appears that the document was, in fact, tendered by Mr. Zecevic. And it has somehow been incorrectly indicated as a Prosecution document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm -- I'm -- I was reminded, just for the sake of -- of clarity on this, I was reminded by my colleague Mr. Cvijetic that the document was MFI'd not because there was an objection by the Prosecution when the document was offered to be tendered, but because the witness said that it -- it -- it is a forgery because the address of the SDA was not -- was not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Okay. Well, now that the address, I believe is -- is -- is resolved, maybe we can re-address the issue again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the document being tendered is now admitted and marked as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I'm so sorry -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I maintain the objection. [Microphone not activated] This witness has never seen the document before. He says he has seen similar documents. I'm maintaining the objection. And particularly in the light of the evidence of Mr. -- I'm asking that a witness be called to give the provenance of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Actually, Ms. Korner, I confess. I had forgotten the answer this witness gave earlier that he had not seen this particular document --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: -- he had seen similar documents. I was acting on the correct -- on the acceptance of the address, which is just one --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: -- which is a different -- related by different -- a different issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm -- I'm saying that I'm going to object to the admission of these documents until I hear from a witness about where these documents come from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The Chamber recalls its earlier order -- order -- that this may be exhibited, and it must remain as an MFI document marked for identification for the time being. Because, as Ms. Korner has correctly reminded us, this witness, although he accepts the correctness of the address, has never seen the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours. I was just -- just notified by -- by my assistants that it was actually Mr. Di Fazio, who asked the document to be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We were reminded of that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Let's not get this confused. It was a mistake to list it as Defence [sic] document. We weren't asking for it to be admitted; we were asking for it to be marked so if we wanted to go back to it, we knew what it was. It's still a -- it's still a Defence document. It's should have never been marked an as a Prosecution document. And that's where the confusion has arisen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It remains marked for identification at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours. I would just -- I would just like to clarify one thing. Maybe it's not the proper time now, but we will have to readdress that, because my understanding of Ms. Korner is that she will object to all the documents, admission of the documents by the Defence until she hears from the witness about where these documents come from. If there is -- if that is the standard, Your Honour, then the Defence will do the same. And I don't think it will bring us to anything reasonable, considering the -- the due process of law and the -- and the normal -- normal procedure in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But, Mr. Zecevic, the -- the so stated, in terms of the -- Ms. Korner's position, that isn't remarkable, is it? We always have to be satisfied as to the provenance of exhibits so that the -- there's no way -- there is no general anticipatory order that that -- that can be made, even with the understanding of counsel. We have to deal with these on an item-by-item basis, as I said earlier. So we'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honours, but I was just -- just surprised by the comment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I wanted to -- I want to make my position absolutely clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I just want to make this very clear. There are certain classes of documents such as those that are taken off a web site from an accused that will be an automatic objection. Other documents, as Your Honours say, we will deal with -- on a case-by-case basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But I have stated that this is not the document -- these are not the documents which come from the web site.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And even if they come from the web site, this is a public domain. The Internet is a public domain, Ms. Korner, and therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It doesn't necessarily follow, with respect, Mr. Zecevic, that because the internet is in a public domain that a document would migrate into the court, if that's the only source. But let's see what happens as we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vlaski, I apologise for the fact that we are losing time. Can we look at 1D124. It's a document of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Croatia training centre, the 31st of July, 1991 is the date. Subject: Attendees of the training course and instructions for those who have left the training course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D124.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever seen the document before or such a document before?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I haven't had the opportunity of seeing this sort of document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the document be -- can the witness be shown 1D00-4704, which is the document dated the 8th of August, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It was also issued about the MUP of Croatia and lists the attendees of the sixth course for individuals training to be policemen. Page 1 is related to the 1st Battalion, which -- the members of which are listed in the alphabetical order. Do you -- can you see the document?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not this particular one. But, as I said earlier, I did see the lists that were sent to Croatia, whereas this particular document was issued in Croatia, and we can't see who it was sent to, but I haven't seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, Mr. Vlaski, these young Muslims who attended -- or who went to the MUP of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, you do know that on their return to the BH they largely joined the reserve force of the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's correct that the SDA leadership, through the MUP reserve force, built up its own armed force which was supposed to acquire legitimacy by virtue of the fact that it was part of an institution which, by its very definition, was an armed forces. And this was a method, the simplest way of creating a powerful armed force through the police reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You must be aware of the fact that the Ministry of the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was illegally arming the Party of Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had information to that effect, and this was more or less known to the public at large, which channels were used for arming.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I have a certain number of receipts here, reflecting the hand-over of weapons and equipment. This is 1D00-6944. The receipts are mostly -- refer to the months of February and March 1992, and they reflect the hand-over of weapons and equipment. Have you ever seen these documents before?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since we had Serb individuals as members of the MUP who worked in certain organisational units which had to do with financial records of the MUP, we received a great deal of information from these individuals, both about the hand-over of weapons and the invoices that were paid in Croatia, Slovenia, and in other countries through certain banks. And behind all of it was Minister Delimustafic, Bruno Stoic, who was the assistant minister and head of finances in MUP. Based on the information thus obtained, we launched information to the media - some of the information was published in the Belgrade media which was not that widely read in Bosnia-Herzegovina - but they were known to the public at large. Now, as for these receipts, specifically, we had a fair amount of information about them because our colleagues who were employed on these posts, in warehouses, and in certain departments were aware of these activities. They even knew of the vehicles used to transport the goods, though I can't tell you exactly where the documentation based on which we were aware of these activities ended up, what became of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, well, he still hasn't answered the question. Can we have an answer, please. Has he ever seen the receipts before was your question. We then got this speech which doesn't answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It was my understanding that he hasn't seen them, and that is why I didn't offer it for -- But I can ask the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you see the receipts that I've just shown you ever before? Have you ever seen them before?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall specific documents. It would really be too much of an expectation to expect me to remember receipt numbers so-and-so. I was aware of some of them; I did see some of them. But receipt number 115, well, almost 20 years later, I can hardly be expected to remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that was my understanding of your answer, but since my learned friend insisted that I repeat the question --

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had I worked in a warehouse where such receipts were issued, I would probably recall them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vlaski. It was because of the nature of your work that you were informed of the secret meeting of the SDA in the police hall which was held on the 26th of May, 1991. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because, at the time, I was the chief of the administration for the security of individuals, and these individuals included Mr. Izetbegovic, who participated in the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At the meeting, a decision was taken, among others, on the setting up of the National Defence Council of the party. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At the meeting held on 26th May, 1991, a decision was taken on the establishment of the Green Berets and the Patriotic League, as paramilitary formations, and on their arming. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not taken in that particular format, but a political decision was made to take that general course. These organisations or formations were not publicly announced at such meetings, not to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The Council for National Defence of the SDA - and we saw, a moment ago, the name Muharemovic, who was the chief of security of the SDA and who authored certain documents - was in fact part of the plan for an armed conflict with a view to separating Bosnia-Herzegovina from Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SDA political leadership did not accept the constitution of the BH in the way in which it was laid down. For any decision of this sort, whereby certain formations which were not provided for by the constitution were set up, since, under the BH constitution, only the JNA was envisaged and the MUP was envisaged as an armed force as well, however, it was under the wing of the party that certain preparations were made for one such activity to be legitimised, whilst taking control of all the leverages of power.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Under the existing rules and regulations, this was an illegal armed rebellion to all intents and purposes?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not call it an illegal rebellion; I would call it illegal preparations. Mr. Izetbegovic was a lawfully elected state official because he was the elected member of the Presidency as a representative of the Bosnian people. So as -- having such a role, he, however, acted as an illegal structure in the Presidency because he was involved in unlawful activities aimed at setting up illegal paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I show you 1D00-4743 now, which is a SDA document, signed by Mr. Hasan Cengic. It bears the date of the 13th June 1991. The document says that -- or notifies the fact that the Council for National Defence was set up. Now officially established as you confirmed to us. This was discussed on the 26th of May.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was on that date that a political decision was taken to set up that formation. It was on that -- at that SDA meeting that a political decision was taken as to what needed to be done. Because the meeting was attended by representatives of the SDA not only of Bosnia-Herzegovina but also of Sandzak, Kosovo, Croatia, Vienna; there were also some foreign emissaries there whose identity we were unable to uncover. It was too difficult a task.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
